entry_sequence.transcript_quote: Our goal here is to identify a P or a B shape profile matching trap scenarios
entry_sequence.action: Identify a P-shape (bullish) or B-shape (bearish) profile, which indicates an area of imbalance (Low Volume Node).
entry_sequence.rationale: These shapes show where the market consolidated or moved quickly through an area of low volume.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: So, you're asking yourself always, what is smart money doing right now? Are they on offense or are they on defense?
entry_sequence.action: Determine if the profile was formed by smart money exiting (defensive move/trap) or entering (offensive move/continuation).
entry_sequence.rationale: Defensive moves (covering/exiting) are likely to fail, creating a trap.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: So, anytime we see a scenario where we think that shorts are trapped, and we see more downwards move, we're not panicking.
entry_sequence.action: Wait for the market to fake out in the direction of the initial bias (the trap).
entry_sequence.rationale: The fakeout is the signal that the opposing side is trapped.

entry_sequence.transcript_quote: you're just going to put your stop right below that point of control
entry_sequence.action: Enter on the reversal/break of the Point of Control (POC) or a key level (VAH/VAL) after the fakeout.
entry_sequence.rationale: The POC failure indicates the initial directional bias is failing.

stop.rationale: The stop is placed below the Point of Control to invalidate the trap.

targets.rationale: The target is the end of the area of imbalance (the vacuum).
